docs.title: DYNAMIXEL-X430-Control-Table-Emulator — any motor as a DYNAMIXEL X430
docs.text: Quick start

docs.title: One joint on one serial line
docs.text:
The application gives the bus a byte writer and feeds it the received bytes; the device calls a hook for every accepted register write, and the motor loop keeps the live registers current. Everything runs in the main loop (or one RX thread).

#include "x430.h"

static struct x430_bus bus;
static struct x430_device joint;

static int uart_write(void* context, const uint8_t* data, size_t length)
{
    (void)context;
    return board_uart_write(data, length); /* 0 on success */
}

static uint8_t on_write(struct x430_device* device, uint16_t address, uint8_t size,
                        int32_t value, void* user_data)
{
    uint8_t result = DXL2_ERR_NONE;

    (void)device;
    (void)size;
    (void)user_data;
    if (address == X430_ADDR_TORQUE_ENABLE)
    {
        if (!motor_enable(value != 0))
        {
            result = DXL2_ERR_RESULT_FAIL; /* the host sees Result Fail */
        }
    }
    else if (address == X430_ADDR_GOAL_POSITION)
    {
        motor_move_to(value);
    }
    else
    {
        /* other registers are only stored */
    }
    return result;
}

static const struct x430_hooks hooks = {.write = on_write};

int main(void)
{
    const struct x430_bus_config bus_config = {.write = uart_write};
    const struct x430_device_config joint_config = {.id = 1U, .hooks = &hooks};

    board_init();
    if ((x430_bus_init(&bus, &bus_config) != X430_OK) ||
        (x430_device_init(&joint, &joint_config) != X430_OK) ||
        (x430_bus_attach(&bus, &joint) != X430_OK))
    {
        for (;;)
        {
        }
    }
    for (;;)
    {
        uint8_t bytes[64];
        const size_t count = board_uart_read(bytes, sizeof(bytes));

        (void)x430_bus_receive(&bus, bytes, count); /* parse, check, hooks, answer */
        if (board_tick_1ms())
        {
            (void)x430_bus_lock(&bus); /* live values from the motor */
            (void)x430_device_set(&joint, X430_ADDR_PRESENT_POSITION, motor_position());
            (void)x430_device_set(&joint, X430_ADDR_MOVING, motor_moving() ? 1 : 0);
            (void)x430_bus_unlock(&bus);
            (void)x430_bus_poll(&bus); /* Bus Watchdog */
        }
    }
}

The board_… and motor_… functions stand for your UART and motor code; the Integration Guide shows the RTOS layout, persistent storage and the port (lock, clock, delay).

Anton Vynohradov · ORCID 0009-0005-6965-0911

docs.title: API Reference
docs.text:
This chapter documents every public function, type and macro of the X430 emulator. Include one header; it declares every function and includes the public type headers:

#include "x430.h"
Header Contents x430.h All public functions, x430_sim_hooks; library version; includes the headers below x430_config.h Build-time configuration (Kconfig or compiler definitions) x430_defs.h Status codes, write options, events, persistent slots, Control Table addresses and values x430_types.h Port, hooks, configuration structures, opaque instances and their sizes x430_model.h Types of the generated model descriptor, x430_model_active x430_model_info.h Generated: name, Model Number and table size of the selected model dxl2.h DXL2-C: DXL2_ERR_* protocol errors, dxl2_write_fn, struct dxl2_packet

Everything else (src/) is private and not installed with the library.

docs.title: Version — x430.h
docs.text: Macro Value Meaning X430_VERSION_MAJOR, …_MINOR, …_PATCH 0, 0, 0 Version numbers; set by CMake from the latest vX.Y.Z tag and stamped into the release package; 0.0.0 means unknown (a header from the repository built without CMake) X430_VERSION "0.0.0" Version string

docs.title: Definitions — x430_defs.h
docs.text:
Status codes (return value of every function):

Macro Value Meaning X430_OK 0 Success X430_ERR_PARAM -1 NULL pointer or a value outside its documented range X430_ERR_STATE -2 Instance not initialized; device already attached X430_ERR_CONFIG -3 Bus full, or the ID is already used on the bus X430_ERR_HAL -4 The byte writer of the bus returned an error X430_ERR_UNSUPPORTED -5 The feature is not compiled in

Write options of x430_device_write() and x430_device_reg_write(): X430_WRITE_SECONDARY (0x01, packet addressed by the Secondary ID: the EEPROM area is locked), X430_WRITE_VALIDATE_ONLY (0x02, check only, store nothing, call no hook).

Events (enum x430_event, argument of the event hook):

Value When Return of the hook X430_EVENT_REBOOT After REBOOT: RAM area reset, errors cleared Ignored X430_EVENT_FACTORY_RESET After FACTORY_RESET (then like REBOOT) Ignored X430_EVENT_CLEAR_MULTI_TURN CLEAR while the device is not moving DXL2_ERR_NONE after bringing Present Position into one turn, or an error for the host X430_EVENT_BUS_WATCHDOG Bus Watchdog expired (Bus Watchdog now reads −1) Ignored X430_EVENT_BAUD_RATE Baud Rate (8) changed; after the status packet Ignored X430_EVENT_TORQUE_SHUTDOWN A hardware error in Shutdown (63) switched the torque off Ignored X430_EVENT_BACKUP_RESTORED BACKUP restore copied the backup into the table Ignored

Persistent slots (enum x430_nvm_slot): X430_NVM_EEPROM (0, X430_NVM_EEPROM_SIZE = 76 bytes), X430_NVM_BACKUP (1, X430_NVM_BACKUP_SIZE = 328 bytes); X430_NVM_HEADER_SIZE = 10.

Control Table constants: X430_ADDR_* (addresses of the registers used by the library and by applications, for example X430_ADDR_GOAL_POSITION = 116, X430_RAM_START = 64), X430_MODE_* (operating modes), X430_DRIVE_MODE_*, X430_STARTUP_*, X430_HW_ERROR_*, X430_MOVING_STATUS_*, the instruction options X430_FACTORY_RESET_*, X430_CLEAR_MULTI_TURN, X430_BACKUP_*, and X430_BUS_WATCHDOG_ERROR, X430_BUS_WATCHDOG_UNIT_MS (20), X430_SECONDARY_ID_DISABLED (253), X430_EXTENDED_POSITION_LIMIT (1,048,575), X430_REALTIME_TICK_PERIOD (32,768), X430_RETURN_DELAY_UNIT_US (2).

docs.title: Types — x430_types.h
docs.text:
Type Members Meaning struct x430_port context, lock, unlock, millis, delay_us Platform services (Configuration) struct x430_hooks write, read, event, nvm_read, nvm_write Application hooks of a device (Using the Library) struct x430_bus_config write, write_context, port Bus configuration struct x430_device_config id, firmware_version, model_information, hooks, user_data Device configuration struct x430_sim_config input_voltage, temperature Simulator configuration

Callback types:

Type Signature Return x430_lock_fn void (*)(void* context) – x430_millis_fn uint32_t (*)(void* context) Milliseconds, wrapping at 2^32 x430_delay_fn void (*)(void* context, uint32_t us) – x430_write_hook uint8_t (*)(struct x430_device* device, uint16_t address, uint8_t size, int32_t value, void* user_data) DXL2_ERR_NONE to accept, a DXL2_ERR_* code to refuse x430_read_hook void (*)(struct x430_device* device, uint16_t address, uint16_t length, void* user_data) – x430_event_hook uint8_t (*)(struct x430_device* device, enum x430_event event, void* user_data) See the events above x430_nvm_read_hook int (*)(struct x430_device* device, enum x430_nvm_slot slot, uint16_t offset, uint8_t* data, uint16_t length, void* user_data) 0 when length bytes from offset were read, negative without data x430_nvm_write_hook int (*)(struct x430_device* device, enum x430_nvm_slot slot, uint16_t offset, const uint8_t* data, uint16_t length, void* user_data) 0, or negative (the remaining parts are not written, the host gets Result Fail)

Instances. struct x430_bus, struct x430_device and struct x430_sim are opaque arrays of X430_BUS_WORDS, X430_DEVICE_WORDS and X430_SIM_WORDS 64-bit words (1,664 B, 384 B and 32 B on Cortex-M4 with the default options). Allocate them, pass their addresses, never read or write their content.

docs.title: Variables — x430.h
docs.text:
extern const struct x430_hooks x430_sim_hooks;

The hooks of the simulated actuator: pass them with x430_device_config::user_data pointing at an initialized struct x430_sim. All members are NULL when X430_FEATURE_SIMULATOR is 0.

docs.title: Functions — x430.h
docs.text: Every function except x430_bus_init(), x430_device_init() and x430_sim_init() returns X430_ERR_STATE for an instance without a successful initialization and then calls no hook. Functions marked lock-free do not take the bus lock: call them from hooks or between x430_bus_lock() and x430_bus_unlock().

docs.title: x430_bus_init
docs.text:
int x430_bus_init(struct x430_bus* bus, const struct x430_bus_config* config);

Initialize a bus. Calls no callback except x430_port::millis.

Parameter Description bus Bus. config Configuration; copied (the port it points at is not). Return Meaning X430_OK Bus ready. X430_ERR_PARAM NULL pointer or no writer.

docs.title: x430_bus_attach
docs.text:
int x430_bus_attach(struct x430_bus* bus, struct x430_device* device);

Attach an initialized device to an initialized bus. Takes the bus lock.

Parameter Description bus Bus. device Device, not attached to any bus. Return Meaning X430_OK Attached. X430_ERR_PARAM NULL pointer. X430_ERR_STATE Bus or device not initialized, or the device is attached. X430_ERR_CONFIG Bus full (X430_MAX_DEVICES) or the ID is used on the bus.

docs.title: x430_bus_receive
docs.text:
int x430_bus_receive(struct x430_bus* bus, const uint8_t* data, size_t length);

Feed received bytes in any chunking; answers every complete instruction packet. Takes the bus lock; runs the hooks.

Parameter Description bus Bus. data Received bytes (may be NULL when length is 0). length Number of bytes. Return Meaning X430_OK Bytes processed. X430_ERR_PARAM NULL bus, or NULL data with a non-zero length. X430_ERR_STATE Bus not initialized. X430_ERR_HAL The writer failed for at least one status packet.

docs.title: x430_bus_handle_packet
docs.text:
int x430_bus_handle_packet(struct x430_bus* bus, const struct dxl2_packet* packet);

Handle one decoded instruction packet, for applications that run their own DXL2-C link. Takes the bus lock; runs the hooks.

Parameter Description bus Bus. packet Packet decoded by DXL2-C. Status packets are ignored. Return Meaning X430_OK Success X430_ERR_PARAM NULL pointer X430_ERR_STATE Bus not initialized X430_ERR_HAL The writer failed

docs.title: x430_bus_poll
docs.text:
int x430_bus_poll(struct x430_bus* bus);

Periodic service: Bus Watchdog of every device. Call every few milliseconds (the watchdog unit is 20 ms). Takes the bus lock.

Parameter Description bus Bus. Return Meaning X430_OK Success X430_ERR_PARAM NULL X430_ERR_STATE Not initialized

docs.title: x430_bus_lock
docs.text:
int x430_bus_lock(struct x430_bus* bus);

Take the bus lock (x430_port::lock; nothing without it). Use it around the live register updates of the application.

Parameter Description bus Bus. Return Meaning X430_OK Success X430_ERR_PARAM NULL X430_ERR_STATE Not initialized

docs.title: x430_bus_unlock
docs.text:
int x430_bus_unlock(struct x430_bus* bus);

Release the bus lock (x430_port::unlock).

Parameter Description bus Bus. Return Meaning X430_OK Success X430_ERR_PARAM NULL X430_ERR_STATE Not initialized

docs.title: x430_bus_find
docs.text:
int x430_bus_find(const struct x430_bus* bus, uint8_t id, struct x430_device** device);

Attached device with the primary ID id (lock-free).

docs.title: x430_device_init
docs.text:
int x430_device_init(struct x430_device* device, const struct x430_device_config* config);

Initialize a device: factory values, stored EEPROM area (nvm_read), the RAM area and the Startup Configuration (which may call the write hook). Initialize a device before x430_bus_attach(), never while a bus serves it: the content of the instance before the call is not trusted (it may be the garbage of a stack instance), so an attachment cannot be detected.

Parameter Description device Device, not attached to a bus. config Configuration; copied (the hooks it points at are not). Return Meaning X430_OK Device ready. X430_ERR_PARAM NULL pointer or ID above 252.

docs.text:

docs.title: How It Works
docs.text: This chapter explains the parts of the X430 emulator, the contexts it runs in, the states of a device, who owns which memory, how errors are reported and what may run in parallel. What a host sees, instruction by instruction, is in X430 Emulation.

docs.title: Modules
docs.text:
Module Files Responsibility Public API x430.h, inc/x430_types.h, inc/x430_defs.h, inc/x430_config.h, inc/x430_model.h Functions, configuration types, hooks, status codes, Control Table addresses, build-time options, the model descriptor type Bus src/x430_bus.c DXL2-C link, addressing (ID, Secondary ID, broadcast), Status Return Level, Return Delay Time, single and group instructions, Fast read packets, Bus Watchdog timing, the bus lock Device src/x430_device.c Control Table image, write checks, write hook and storage, Indirect Address, REG_WRITE/ACTION, REBOOT, FACTORY_RESET, CLEAR, BACKUP, hardware errors, persistent blocks Model <build>/x430/generated/x430_model_table.c, x430_model_info.h The register list and address map of the selected model, written by tools/x430_gen_model.py from models/ Simulator src/x430_sim.c Kinematic model of the actuator behind a device (optional) DXL2-C dependency Protocol 2.0 parser, encoder, CRC-16, byte stuffing

Only the public API is visible to the application. Everything under src/ is private: the instances struct x430_bus, struct x430_device and struct x430_sim are opaque blocks of memory whose layout may change in any release.

docs.title: Execution contexts
docs.text:
Bus context Motor context Functions x430_bus_receive(), x430_bus_handle_packet(), x430_bus_poll() x430_bus_lock(), x430_device_set() / x430_device_get(), x430_bus_unlock(), x430_sim_step() Context One RX thread or the main loop, never an interrupt The motor control loop (task or main loop) Rate As bytes arrive; x430_bus_poll() every 5–20 ms The rate of the control loop (for example 1 kHz) Work Parse, check, call the hooks, store, answer Copy the motor state into the live registers Time Bounded by the packet: loops over its parameters, the touched registers, the devices of the bus Bounded; x430_sim_step() is proportional to its elapsed_ms

The two contexts share the Control Tables. The bus functions take the bus lock (x430_port::lock) for the whole packet; the motor context takes the same lock around its updates with x430_bus_lock(). On bare metal both run in the main loop and the port has no lock.

Hooks run inside the bus context with the lock held. A hook may call the lock-free device functions (x430_device_get(), x430_device_set(), x430_device_id(), x430_device_raise_hardware_error()) but no bus function; to hand work to another thread, post to an application queue from the hook.

docs.title: States
docs.text:
State Torque Enable (64) Entered by Left by Not initialized – a zeroed or never initialized instance x430_device_init() Torque off 0 initialization, REBOOT, a write of 0, a shutdown a write of 1, Startup Configuration bit 0, a goal write with Drive Mode bit 3 Torque on 1 the transitions above; Goal Position takes Present Position a write of 0, a hardware error in Shutdown (63) Shutdown 0, locked x430_device_raise_hardware_error() with a bit enabled in Shutdown REBOOT (Hardware Error Status cleared) Watchdog error 1, Bus Watchdog reads −1 no instruction packet for Bus Watchdog × 20 ms a write of Bus Watchdog

While a hardware error bit is set, every status packet carries the alert bit (0x80).

docs.title: Memory model
docs.text:
Object Owner Size on Cortex-M4 Lifetime struct x430_bus Application (static, stack or pool) 1,664 B (768-byte packets, the default), 640 B (256-byte packets) From x430_bus_init() struct x430_device Application 384 B (with every feature and without) From x430_device_init() struct x430_sim Application 32 B From x430_sim_init() Configurations Application; copied by the *_init() functions – Only during the call Hooks (struct x430_hooks), port (struct x430_port) Application – As long as the device or bus (the library keeps a pointer) Model table Library (const, flash) 921 B Static

A device holds the compact image of its Control Table (316 bytes: the 662 addresses without their long reserved runs, theory) and the REG_WRITE data (X430_REG_WRITE_SIZE); it keeps no copy of a persistent block, the hooks read and write blocks in parts. A bus holds the DXL2-C link (receive buffer and decoded packet) and one packet buffer in which it builds and byte-stuffs every status packet, Fast Sync/Bulk Read answers included. There is no heap, no global or static mutable variable and no hidden buffer: the sizes are fixed at compile time by X430_BUS_WORDS, X430_DEVICE_WORDS and X430_SIM_WORDS (plain arithmetic of the configuration macros, which static analysis can evaluate) and checked against the private state by _Static_assert.

docs.title: Error handling
docs.text:
Situation Result NULL instance or argument X430_ERR_PARAM; nothing is changed A device ID above 252, a bus without writer x430_device_init() / x430_bus_init() return X430_ERR_PARAM; the instance is not changed Any call before a successful initialization X430_ERR_STATE; no hook is called Attaching a device twice X430_ERR_STATE Bus full, ID already used on the bus X430_ERR_CONFIG The byte writer returns non-zero x430_bus_receive() / x430_bus_handle_packet() return X430_ERR_HAL (once) A feature that is not compiled in X430_ERR_UNSUPPORTED (x430_device_backup(), x430_sim_*()) An instruction the device refuses X430_OK; the protocol error (DXL2_ERR_*) goes into the status packet and into the error output Malformed packet (CRC, length) Dropped by DXL2-C; no answer, as a real device

Instruction semantics never fail at the API level: an invalid address, length or value is a protocol error for the host, not an error of the application.

docs.title: Threading and reentrancy
docs.text:
• Per bus: one bus context; the bus functions are not reentrant for the same bus.
  • Live register updates from another context go between x430_bus_lock() and x430_bus_unlock(); the lock must be recursive if a hook can lead to code that takes it again.
  • Different buses share nothing and may run in parallel.
  • Hooks run in the context of the bus function that calls them.

docs.title: Design decisions
docs.text: Decision Reason One model per build, generated tables The Control Table is data (YAML checked against the e-Manual), not code; a build carries only the table it needs. Library = table and protocol, motor = application The same library serves steppers, BLDC drives and the simulator; motion control has no place in a protocol emulator. Two passes for a write: check every register, then hook and store A multi-register write is all or nothing for the checks, as on the real actuator. Hooks receive real addresses Indirect Data is resolved by the library; the application needs one write path. Status codes for API misuse, DXL2_ERR_* for the host Errors of the application and errors of the host never mix. Persistent blocks with header and CRC A block from another model, format or a damaged flash page is ignored; the device starts with factory values. Opaque instances The application cannot depend on internal fields (MISRA deviation DEV-01). X430_ERR_STATE before initialization A zeroed or garbage instance never calls a NULL hook.

docs.title: Changelog
docs.text: All notable changes to this project are documented here. The format follows Keep a Changelog and versions follow Semantic Versioning.
Less RAM per bus with DXL2-C 2.0.0. The public API is unchanged; the instance of a bus is smaller, so code built against 1.1.0 must be recompiled.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• DXL2-C 2.0.0 (was 1.0.0, X430_DXL2_GIT_TAG): the parser removes the byte stuffing in place, and the decoded packet points into its receive buffer instead of holding a copy of the parameters. X430_DXL2_LINK_BYTES follows the new struct dxl2_link.
  • DXL2_MAX_PACKET_SIZE has one default per build system: Kconfig.x430 and x430.cmake (768). x430_config.h no longer sets its own default; a build without Kconfig, without x430.cmake and without the definition stops with #error instead of using a size DXL2-C may not have been compiled with.

docs.title: Quality
docs.text:
• Cortex-M4 (arm-none-eabi-gcc 13.2.1, -Os, XM430-W350): 1,664 B RAM per bus with 768-byte packets (was 2,424 B), 640 B with 256-byte packets (was 888 B); 384 B per device and 32 B per simulator as before. Flash 10,119 B with the model table (was 10,191 B), DXL2-C 842 B (was 850 B). Worst-case stack unchanged (424 B, x430_bus_receive()).
  • The unit tests (138 CTest tests, 105 without the optional features) with 100 % line and branch coverage of src/, all 17 models, the DynamixelSDK end-to-end check and MISRA C:2012 (0 violations, Cppcheck 2.13) pass with DXL2-C 2.0.0.
Several emulator buses on one wire: one bus per MCU, connected to one half-duplex DYNAMIXEL bus (for example one stepper drive per joint), now behave like X series actuators on that wire.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• SYNC_READ and BULK_READ take turns: a hosted device answers only after the status packet of the ID listed just before it in the request (at once after a device of the same bus). The bus now decodes the status packets of other devices on the wire for this. Before, every hosted device answered at once and IDs of other buses were skipped, so the answers of several buses collided on a shared wire.
  • If that status does not arrive within X430_TURN_TIMEOUT_MS, or the host sends its next instruction first, or a hosted device does not answer reads (Status Return Level 0), the remaining hosted devices of the read stay silent.
  • FAST_SYNC_READ and FAST_BULK_READ: when the request lists an ID that the bus does not host, the bus stays silent (one bus cannot build the chained answer of several), and the ROBOTIS ROS 2 hardware interface falls back to SYNC_READ. Before, the bus answered for its own IDs only, which the host decoded as a malformed answer. With all IDs on one bus nothing changes.
  • struct x430_bus grows by the pending read: 2,424 B on Cortex-M4 with the default options (was 2,368 B); x430_bus.c 3,090 B flash at -Os (was 2,820 B). The stack of every public function is unchanged. Rebuild the application with the new headers.

docs.title: Added
docs.text: • X430_TURN_TIMEOUT_MS / CONFIG_X430_TURN_TIMEOUT_MS (default 100 ms, 1..60000): the longest wait for the status of the ID before, from the last progress of the read.
First release: device-side emulation of DYNAMIXEL X430 actuators over Protocol 2.0. The public API (x430.h and inc/) is stable within major version 1.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• Bus (struct x430_bus): decodes the instruction packets of one serial line with DXL2-C 1.0.0 and answers for up to X430_MAX_DEVICES devices. PING, READ, WRITE, REG_WRITE, ACTION, FACTORY_RESET, REBOOT, CLEAR, BACKUP, SYNC_READ/WRITE, BULK_READ/WRITE, FAST_SYNC_READ and FAST_BULK_READ; broadcast, Secondary ID, Status Return Level, Return Delay Time, Bus Watchdog. x430_bus_handle_packet() for applications with their own DXL2-C link.
  • Device (struct x430_device): the Control Table of the model selected at build time with the rules of the real actuator: access rights, ranges and limit registers, EEPROM lock while the torque is on, all-or-nothing checks of multi-register writes, Indirect Address/Data, hardware error shutdown and alert bit, Startup Configuration, Drive Mode "torque on by goal update", Goal Position := Present Position on torque on, factory reset, reboot, multi-turn clear and Control Table backup.
  • Application hooks per device (write, read, event, nvm_read, nvm_write) and an optional platform port (lock, millisecond clock, delay). Persistent blocks carry a header (model, format, slot, size) and a CRC-16; a foreign or damaged block is ignored. The device reads and writes them in parts at an offset and keeps no copy of a block in RAM.
  • Memory layout for small MCUs: a device keeps a compact image of its Control Table (316 of 662 bytes: the long reserved runs are left out); the bus builds every status packet in one buffer and stuffs it in place (no packet buffer on the stack); the model table has no address map and generates the 56 Indirect Address registers from the indirect blocks. A status whose byte-stuffed form exceeds DXL2_MAX_PACKET_SIZE is answered with a Data Length Error.
  • All 17 X430 models (XM430-W350/W210, XH430-W350/W210/V350/V210, XD430-T350/T210, XW430-T333/T200, XL430-W250, 2XL430-W250, XC430-W150/W240/T150BB/T240BB, 2XC430-W250): Control Tables generated from models/*.yaml and checked against the ROBOTIS e-Manual tables. Application overrides of the model (X430_MODEL_OVERRIDES / CONFIG_X430_MODEL_OVERRIDES), for example a supply above 16 V. The generator needs only the Python standard library (PyYAML is used when installed).
  • Simulator (struct x430_sim, x430_sim_hooks): a kinematic model with the X430 velocity profiles for tests and for setting up a system without hardware; POSIX host simulator examples/host_sim serving simulated devices on a serial port or pseudo-terminal.
  • Configuration with plain compiler definitions (COMPILE_DEFINITIONS) or, when X430_KCONFIG is switched on, Kconfig (Kconfiglib, menuconfig); optional features BULK, FAST_READ, BACKUP and SIMULATOR; COMPILE_OPTIONS for the flags of the library sources. Packets of up to 768 bytes by default, so a host can read the whole Control Table at once (DYNAMIXEL Wizard).
  • UNIT_TESTS builds the unit tests also when the library is a submodule of another project (executable x430_gtest, CTest label x430); the x430 library never contains them.
  • Opaque, caller-owned instances; every function returns X430_OK or an X430_ERR_* code (PARAM, STATE, CONFIG, HAL, UNSUPPORTED) and refuses an instance without a successful initialization. Protocol errors go to the host in the status packet.
  • Documentation website and PDF user manual: overview, architecture, usage, the emulated device in detail, integration (UART, RTOS, flash, ROS 2, DYNAMIXEL Wizard), API reference, MISRA deviation register.

docs.title: Quality
docs.text:
• Cortex-M4 (arm-none-eabi-gcc 13.2.1, -Os, XM430-W350, 768-byte packets): 384 B RAM per device, 2,368 B per bus (832 B with 256-byte packets), 32 B per simulator; 9,921 B flash with the model table (+850 B DXL2-C); .data and .bss empty; worst-case stack 424 B (x430_bus_receive(), with any packet size).
  • 131 GoogleTest cases with 100 % line and branch coverage of src/, and 100 cases with 100 % without the optional features; unit tests for all 17 models; model data against the e-Manual; 52 checks end to end with the official ROBOTIS DynamixelSDK; the simulator's trapezoidal move within 0.7 % of the closed form.
  • MISRA C:2012: 0 violations with Cppcheck 2.13, deviations DEV-01 (Rule 11.3, opaque instances) and DEV-02 (Rule 11.5, callback contexts). No warnings with -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -Wconversion; AddressSanitizer and UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer clean.
  • Verified on hardware: a stepper joint firmware (STM32G431, Zephyr) emulating an XM430-W350 with DYNAMIXEL Wizard 2.0.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text: The X430 emulator has two kinds of configuration. Build-time options select the emulated model, the sizes and the optional instructions; they come from Kconfig or from plain compiler definitions and end up as macros of inc/x430_config.h. Run-time configuration is the content of struct x430_bus_config, struct x430_device_config and struct x430_sim_config, passed to the *_init() functions. This chapter lists both, then the memory footprint and the measured stack usage.

docs.title: Build-time options
docs.text:
Kconfig symbol Macro Default Range Meaning X430_MODEL_* (choice) X430_MODEL_NAME, X430_MODEL_IS_<KEY> XM430-W350 17 models Emulated model (one per build); CMake X430_MODEL without Kconfig X430_MODEL_NUMBER_OVERRIDE X430_MODEL_NUMBER 0 = documented number 0..65535 Model Number reported by PING and address 0 X430_MODEL_OVERRIDES – empty file YAML file of application overrides of the model (below) X430_FIRMWARE_VERSION X430_FIRMWARE_VERSION 52 1..255 Firmware Version (6) when the device configuration gives 0 X430_MAX_DEVICES X430_MAX_DEVICES 4 1..253 Devices (IDs) per bus X430_REG_WRITE_SIZE X430_REG_WRITE_SIZE 32 4..662 Largest REG_WRITE data per device, bytes X430_BAUD_RATE_CODE_MAX X430_BAUD_RATE_CODE_MAX 7 7..255 Highest Baud Rate (8) code a write accepts X430_TURN_TIMEOUT_MS X430_TURN_TIMEOUT_MS 100 1..60000 Shared bus: longest wait for the status of the ID before a hosted device in a SYNC_READ / BULK_READ (group instructions) X430_DXL2_MAX_PACKET_SIZE DXL2_MAX_PACKET_SIZE (DXL2-C) 768 64..4096 Largest packet; limits READ length and Fast read answers X430_BULK X430_FEATURE_BULK y y/n BULK_READ, BULK_WRITE X430_FAST_READ X430_FEATURE_FAST_READ y y/n FAST_SYNC_READ, FAST_BULK_READ X430_BACKUP X430_FEATURE_BACKUP y y/n BACKUP, Backup Ready, Startup RAM Restore X430_SIMULATOR X430_FEATURE_SIMULATOR y y/n x430_sim

The ranges are those of Kconfig.x430; without Kconfig, x430_config.h checks X430_MAX_DEVICES and X430_REG_WRITE_SIZE with #error and DXL2-C checks its packet size. The application must be compiled with the same values as the library; with CMake they are public compile definitions of the x430 target.

Without Kconfig (the default) the options are compiler definitions, given in the CMake variable COMPILE_DEFINITIONS; compiler options of the library sources (optimization, CPU flags) go into COMPILE_OPTIONS. Both names have no prefix on purpose: a project sets them once for all the libraries it includes.

docs.title: With Kconfig
docs.text:
With X430_KCONFIG=ON (off by default; preset X430[Kconfig]), Kconfiglib merges the fragments of X430_CONF_FILES (default configs/defconfig) into <build>/x430/.config and writes x430_autoconf.h. As long as the fragments do not change, the existing .config is kept, so values chosen in menuconfig survive.

cmake --preset "X430[Kconfig]"
cmake --build "build/X430[Kconfig]" --target menuconfig      # terminal UI
cmake --build "build/X430[Kconfig]" --target savedefconfig   # minimal fragment
cmake -S . -B build -DX430_CONF_FILES="$PWD/configs/defconfig;$PWD/my_robot.conf"

# my_robot.conf
CONFIG_X430_MODEL_XW430_T333=y
CONFIG_X430_MAX_DEVICES=6
CONFIG_X430_BACKUP=n

A project with its own Kconfig tree switches X430_KCONFIG on, points X430_KCONFIG_ROOT at its top-level Kconfig and sources Kconfig.x430 from it. An RTOS with its own Kconfig (Zephyr) keeps X430_KCONFIG off: the application Kconfig sources Kconfig.x430 and the glue passes the CONFIG_X430_* values to the CMake variables.

docs.title: Without Kconfig
docs.text:
Without Kconfig only Python 3 is needed. Every optional feature is on unless defined to 0; options are compiler definitions, given in COMPILE_DEFINITIONS:

cmake -S . -B build -DX430_MODEL=xl430_w250 \
    -DCOMPILE_DEFINITIONS="X430_MAX_DEVICES=8U;X430_FEATURE_BACKUP=0" -DCOMPILE_OPTIONS="-Os"

docs.title: Packet size
docs.text:
DXL2_MAX_PACKET_SIZE limits the length of a READ answer to DXL2_MAX_PACKET_SIZE − 11 bytes and the size of a Fast read answer to DXL2_MAX_PACKET_SIZE bytes (10 + devices × (bytes + 4)). The default is 768: a READ of up to 757 bytes, so a host can read the whole Control Table (addresses 0–661, 662 bytes) at once, as DYNAMIXEL Wizard 2.0 does (with 256 it gets a Data Length Error and shows TIME OUT). A product whose hosts read less may lower it: with 256 the bus needs 640 B instead of 1,664 B (the stack does not depend on the packet size: the bus builds its answers in its own buffer).

The default has two places, one per build system: CONFIG_X430_DXL2_MAX_PACKET_SIZE in Kconfig.x430 and the cache variable X430_DXL2_MAX_PACKET_SIZE in x430.cmake, which gives it to DXL2-C as a public compiler definition, so the library, its tests and the application that links x430 all see the same value. x430_config.h has no default of its own and stops a build that sets neither. Without CMake, define DXL2_MAX_PACKET_SIZE (for example -DDXL2_MAX_PACKET_SIZE=768U) for the library, DXL2-C and the application alike; the default of DXL2-C alone is 256.

docs.title: Application overrides of the model
docs.text:
A product built on the emulator may need another range or initial value than the ROBOTIS model, for example a supply above the 16 V of an XM430. Instead of editing models/, give a YAML file with the same overrides: mapping as the model files:

overrides:
  Max Voltage Limit: {min: 95, max: 300}
  Min Voltage Limit: {min: 95, max: 300}

Set its path in CONFIG_X430_MODEL_OVERRIDES or in the CMake cache variable X430_MODEL_OVERRIDES. tools/x430_gen_model.py --overrides <file> applies it after the model file; an unknown register name or an initial value outside the resulting range stops the build.

docs.title: Run-time configuration
docs.text: The *_init() functions copy the structures, so they may be temporaries or const in flash. The hooks and the port they point at are not copied: keep them alive.

docs.title: struct x430_bus_config
docs.text: Field Required Meaning write Yes int write(void* context, const uint8_t* data, size_t length): writes one complete status packet; returns 0, or non-zero on error (reported as X430_ERR_HAL) write_context – Passed to write port – struct x430_port: platform services, NULL for none

docs.text: Member Called from Used for NULL means context – Passed to every member – lock, unlock Bus functions, x430_bus_lock(), x430_bus_unlock(), x430_sim_step() Mutual exclusion of the Control Tables Single context (bare metal) millis Bus functions, x430_device_read() Realtime Tick (120), Bus Watchdog Tick 0, no watchdog timeout delay_us Before each status packet Return Delay Time (9) × 2 µs Status sent at once

docs.text: Field Unit Default (0) Meaning input_voltage 0.1 V 120 (12.0 V) Present Input Voltage (144) temperature °C 30 Present Temperature (146)

docs.title: Memory footprint
docs.text:
Measured with tools/x430_measure.sh and arm-none-eabi-gcc 13.2.1 for Cortex-M4 (-mcpu=cortex-m4 -mthumb), model XM430-W350, X430_MAX_DEVICES 4, X430_REG_WRITE_SIZE 32, DXL2_MAX_PACKET_SIZE 768:

Object All features No optional feature struct x430_device (RAM per device) 384 B 384 B struct x430_bus (RAM per bus) 1,664 B 1,664 B struct x430_bus, DXL2_MAX_PACKET_SIZE 256 640 B 640 B struct x430_sim 32 B – .data + .bss 0 B 0 B

A device is its compact Control Table image (316 B), the REG_WRITE data (X430_REG_WRITE_SIZE, 32 B) and its state; it keeps no copy of a persistent block. A bus is the DXL2-C link (receive buffer, in which DXL2-C 2.0.0 also decodes the packet: 804 B with 768-byte packets), one packet buffer for its answers (DXL2_MAX_PACKET_SIZE), the device list (X430_MAX_DEVICES pointers) and the pending SYNC_READ / BULK_READ of a shared bus (X430_MAX_DEVICES entries of 12 B). The optional features change code, not RAM.

Flash (.text, including constants) per module:

Module -Os -O2 -Os, no optional feature x430_device.c 4,158 B 5,916 B 3,814 B x430_bus.c 3,018 B 4,132 B 2,242 B x430_sim.c 2,022 B 2,364 B 32 B x430_model_table.c (XM430-W350) 921 B 921 B 921 B Library 10,119 B 13,333 B 7,009 B DXL2-C (dxl2_protocol.c, dxl2_link.c) 842 B 980 B 842 B

The model table holds 55 registers of 16 bytes, the two Indirect Address blocks (the library generates their 56 registers) and the three segments of the image; a register is found by binary search. DXL2-C is listed as compiled: the bus uses only its parser and dxl2_crc16(), so a link with --gc-sections drops dxl2_link_send() and dxl2_link_send_status().

On the x86-64 host the device needs 392 B and the bus 2,488 B (64-bit pointers).

docs.title: Stack usage
docs.text:
Worst-case stack of each public function including the library and DXL2-C functions it calls, measured with -fstack-usage -fcallgraph-info=su and tools/docs/stack_usage.py. The packet handler and the byte writer that DXL2-C calls through function pointers are included; the application's hooks, port functions and byte writer are not — add their stack to the function that calls them.

Function Cortex-M4 -Os Cortex-M4 -O0 -Os, packet 256 x430_bus_init() 48 104 48 x430_bus_attach() 40 104 40 x430_bus_receive() 424 656 424 x430_bus_handle_packet() 392 600 392 x430_bus_poll() 32 104 32 x430_bus_lock(), x430_bus_unlock() 8 64 8 x430_bus_find() 40 104 40 x430_device_init() 136 208 136 x430_device_get() 92 144 92 x430_device_set() 92 144 92 x430_device_id() 16 96 16 x430_device_raise_hardware_error() 20 72 20 x430_device_flush_events() 20 72 20 x430_device_read() 112 136 112 x430_device_write() 256 384 256 x430_device_reg_write() 264 384 264 x430_device_action() 248 384 248 x430_device_reboot() 128 200 128 x430_device_factory_reset() 144 216 144 x430_device_clear() 108 176 108 x430_device_backup() 120 192 120 x430_sim_init() 16 80 16 x430_sim_step() 284 680 284

The deepest chain of x430_bus_receive() is a REG_WRITE: dispatch, the write of the device (the written bytes merged with Indirect Data resolved). No packet-sized buffer is on the stack: the bus builds and byte-stuffs each status packet in place in its own buffer, and the device reads and writes persistent blocks in parts (a 16-byte chunk on the stack while it checks a block). Give the bus context this figure plus its hooks.

To re-measure (in a configured build directory):

tools/x430_measure.sh "build/X430[Release]"
