docs.title: Extending the Library
docs.text: Most extensions are built on top of the API: a motor behind the hooks, other devices on the same line, a product-specific range of a register. This chapter shows where each belongs and the rules for changes to the library itself.

docs.title: Where to extend
docs.text: You want to… Do it in Library change needed? Run on another MCU, UART or RTOS The byte writer, the port and the RX code No Drive another kind of motor The hooks of the device No Change a range or an initial value of the model (for example a supply above 16 V) An application overrides file (Configuration) No Report your firmware version to the host x430_device_config::model_information (Model Information, 2) No Accept more Baud Rate codes X430_BAUD_RATE_CODE_MAX (in COMPILE_DEFINITIONS or Kconfig) and a check in the write hook No Host other, non-X430 devices on the same line Your own DXL2-C link and x430_bus_handle_packet() (below) No Answer for registers beyond the X430 table Your own router before the bus (below) No Add an X430 model models/x430/<model>.yaml, Kconfig.x430, the e-Manual snapshot Model data only Emulate another DYNAMIXEL family models/<family>_family.yaml and its models Model data; the addresses of x430_defs.h must match A new instruction src/x430_bus.c Yes

docs.title: Several kinds of devices on one line
docs.text:
An application that already runs its own DXL2-C link — for example to host a controller device with its own Control Table next to the joints — routes the packets itself and hands the rest to the bus:

#define CONTROLLER_ID 200U

void controller_handle(const struct dxl2_packet* packet);

static void on_packet(const struct dxl2_packet* packet, void* context)
{
    (void)context;
    if (packet->id == CONTROLLER_ID)
    {
        controller_handle(packet);
    }
    else
    {
        (void)x430_bus_handle_packet(&bus, packet); /* answers through the bus writer */
    }
}

The same router can answer READs of an address window beyond the 662-byte X430 table (a driver register window, for example) before the bus sees them; the bus would answer them with an Access Error.

docs.title: Adding a model
docs.text:
1. Write models/x430/<model>.yaml with the differences from models/x430_family.yaml (copy a similar model): Model Number, variant (current or load), operating modes, removed registers, initial values and ranges.
  2. Add the choice entry and the X430_MODEL_NAME default to Kconfig.x430 (tests/models fails if it is missing).
  3. Add the e-Manual rows to tests/models/emanual_x430.json.
  4. Run the unit tests with -DX430_MODEL=<model>.

python3 tools/x430_gen_model.py --models-dir models --dump <model> prints the resolved table.

docs.title: Contributing to the library
docs.text:
1. Code. C11, no new dependencies, no heap, no global state; the rules of misra-analyze; internal types stay in src/, x430.h declares the public API only.
  2. Tests. 100 % line and branch coverage of src/ in every unit test preset (X430[UnitTests], X430[UnitTestsMinimal]); the test binary also passes in one process.
  3. Instance size. If a private state grows, update the arithmetic of X430_BUS_BYTES, X430_DEVICE_BYTES or X430_SIM_BYTES in inc/x430_types.h; the build fails until it fits, and a unit test fails if it wastes a word.
  4. Analysis. misra-analyze 0 violations with Cppcheck 2.13, or a recorded deviation in MISRA C:2012.
  5. Format. clang-format 18 reports no changes.
  6. Documentation. The affected pages, the measured figures (tools/x430_measure.sh), the diagrams and CHANGELOG.md [Unreleased].
  7. Compatibility. The public API is stable within a major version.

docs.title: Getting Started
docs.text: This chapter shows how to get the X430 emulator, add it to your project, and build and test it.

docs.title: Get the library
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/AntonVynohradov/DYNAMIXEL-X430-Control-Table-Emulator.git

Each release provides the source code, a prebuilt static library for Linux x86-64 (default options: XM430-W350, every feature) with its headers, the MISRA report and the PDF user manual. For an MCU, and for any other model, build the library from source: the Control Table is generated for the model chosen at build time.

docs.title: Add it to your project
docs.text:
CMake.

set(X430_MODEL xm430_w350)        # X430_KCONFIG ON for Kconfig fragments, see Configuration
include(path/to/DYNAMIXEL-X430-Control-Table-Emulator/x430.cmake)
target_link_libraries(app PRIVATE x430)

x430.cmake generates the Control Table of the model into the build directory, fetches DXL2-C 2.0.0 with FetchContent (or takes a local checkout given in FETCHCONTENT_SOURCE_DIR_DXL2) and defines the static library x430, which links dxl2.

Any other build system. Run python3 tools/x430_gen_model.py --models-dir models --model xm430_w350 --out-dir gen, compile src/*.c, gen/x430_model_table.c and the two sources of DXL2-C, and add the repository root, inc/, gen/ and the DXL2-C folders to the include path. Pass the same X430_* definitions to the library and the application, and define DXL2_MAX_PACKET_SIZE=768U for the library, DXL2-C and the application alike (x430_config.h has no default and stops the build without it).

As a submodule with tests. A project that sets UNIT_TESTS=ON also builds the unit tests of this library (x430_gtest, CTest label x430); COMPILE_DEFINITIONS and COMPILE_OPTIONS of the project reach the library as well.

docs.title: Prerequisites for development
docs.text:
• C11 compiler, CMake 3.20+, Python 3 (the model generator needs only the standard library; PyYAML is used when installed)
  • Optional: GoogleTest and gcovr, Cppcheck 2.13, clang-format 18, Kconfiglib, Python 3 with requirements-dev.txt (MkDocs, WeasyPrint, ziamath), Doxygen, Pango, arm-none-eabi-gcc for the measurements

docs.title: Build with presets
docs.text:
Preset Purpose X430[Debug] Static library with debug information (XM430-W350, without Kconfig) X430[Release] Optimized static library X430[UnitTests] GoogleTest suite with coverage, every feature; target coverage X430[UnitTestsMinimal] The same with every optional feature left out X430[Kconfig] Configuration with Kconfiglib and configs/defconfig; target menuconfig X430[Examples] x430_host_sim, the POSIX host simulator 
cmake --preset "X430[Debug]"
cmake --build "build/X430[Debug]"

Another model: cmake --preset "X430[Debug]" -DX430_MODEL=xl430_w250.

docs.title: Unit tests and coverage
docs.text:
cmake --preset "X430[UnitTests]"
cmake --build "build/X430[UnitTests]" --target coverage

The coverage target runs the tests and fails below X430_COVERAGE_MIN (100 %) line or branch coverage of src/. Both unit test presets reach 100 %. The tests are in tests/unit/ (one file per area: API contract, protocol, group instructions, lifecycle, device rules, simulator); tests/compile/x430_api_check.c compiles the public API alone, as an application sees it. CTest also runs tests/models, which compares the model data with the e-Manual tables.

End to end with the official DynamixelSDK (Linux):

cmake --preset "X430[Examples]" && cmake --build "build/X430[Examples]"
tests/sdk/run_sdk_check.sh "build/X430[Examples]"

The script clones the ROBOTIS DynamixelSDK, serves three simulated devices on a pseudo-terminal and runs 52 checks: PING, READ/WRITE, Sync, Bulk and Fast reads, Indirect Address, REBOOT, FACTORY_RESET, CLEAR.

docs.title: Static analysis
docs.text:
Target Tool cppcheck-analyze Cppcheck, all checks misra-analyze Cppcheck MISRA C:2012 addon; fails on any violation codeql-analyze CodeQL cpp-queries

Check MISRA with the Cppcheck version of CI (2.13, Ubuntu 24.04): newer versions and Windows hosts report other findings.

docs.title: Formatting
docs.text:
clang-format -i x430.h inc/*.h src/*.c src/*.h tests/unit/*.cpp tests/unit/*.h \
    tests/compile/*.c examples/host_sim/*.c

CI checks every C/C++ file with clang-format 18.

docs.title: Versioning and releases
docs.text:
The X430 emulator follows Semantic Versioning: the public API (x430.h and inc/) is stable within a major version. The version comes only from the latest vX.Y.Z Git tag: cmake/version.cmake sets it in CMake builds and the release workflow stamps it into the packaged x430.h. A header taken from the repository and built without CMake reports 0.0.0 (unknown). Every change is recorded under [Unreleased] in CHANGELOG.md.

A release tag runs release.yml: changelog check, version stamp, unit tests with the coverage gate in every unit test preset, MISRA gate, release build, and a GitHub Release with the static library, the headers, the MISRA report and the PDF manual.

docs.title: Measured figures
docs.text: tools/x430_measure.sh <build-dir> [dxl2-dir] prints every figure of the Configuration chapter: the instance sizes on Cortex-M4 and on the host, the flash of each module and the worst-case stack of every public function.

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text: Task Command VS Code task Live preview mkdocs serve Docs: Serve on localhost Build the website mkdocs build Docs: Build site Build the PDF manual python tools/docs/build_manual.py Docs: Build PDF manual Regenerate diagrams python tools/docs/diagrams.py Docs: Generate diagrams Compile the C snippets python tools/docs/check_snippets.py (after configuring X430[Debug]) Docs: Check C snippets

docs.title: Integration Guide
docs.text:
The X430 emulator does not touch hardware. An integration has four parts:

  1. Input: the bytes received on the DYNAMIXEL line (TTL half duplex or RS-485), passed to x430_bus_receive() in any chunking.
  2. Output: the byte writer of struct x430_bus_config, which sends one complete status packet (and switches the direction of a half-duplex line).
  3. The motor: the hooks of each device and the live register updates.
  4. Contexts and storage: the port (lock, millisecond clock, delay) and the persistent blocks.

docs.title: Timing
docs.text: Item Requirement x430_bus_receive() As soon as bytes arrive; a status packet is sent from inside the call Return Delay Time (9) Waited through x430_port::delay_us (default 250 × 2 µs = 500 µs) x430_bus_poll() Every 5–20 ms (Bus Watchdog unit 20 ms) Live register updates At the rate of the control loop, between x430_bus_lock() and x430_bus_unlock() Interrupts Never call a library function from an interrupt handler: the UART interrupt only stores bytes Stack of the bus context 424 B on Cortex-M4 -Os (with any packet size), plus the hooks (Configuration)

docs.title: Bare metal
docs.text:
static int uart_write(void* context, const uint8_t* data, size_t length)
{
    (void)context;
    return board_uart_write(data, length);
}

static uint32_t millis(void* context)
{
    (void)context;
    return board_millis();
}

static void delay_us(void* context, uint32_t us)
{
    (void)context;
    board_delay_us(us);
}

static const struct x430_port port = {
    .context = NULL, .lock = NULL, .unlock = NULL, .millis = millis, .delay_us = delay_us};

void serve_forever(void)
{
    for (;;)
    {
        uint8_t bytes[64];
        const size_t count = board_uart_read(bytes, sizeof(bytes)); /* from the RX ring */

        (void)x430_bus_receive(&bus, bytes, count);
        if (board_tick_1ms())
        {
            (void)x430_device_set(&joint, X430_ADDR_PRESENT_POSITION, motor_position());
            (void)x430_bus_poll(&bus);
        }
    }
}

bus and joint are set up as in Using the Library with .port = &port. Without a lock everything runs in the main loop.

docs.title: RTOS
docs.text:
UART ISR --bytes--> ring buffer --> RX thread: x430_bus_receive()   (lock held inside)
                                        `- hooks --commands--> queue --> motor thread
motor thread: x430_bus_lock(); x430_device_set(Present ...); x430_bus_unlock();
timer or RX thread: x430_bus_poll() every 5-20 ms

The lock must be recursive if a hook can lead to code that takes it again. Zephyr mutexes are recursive:

static void lock(void* context)
{
    mutex_lock(context); /* Zephyr: k_mutex_lock(context, K_FOREVER) */
}

static void unlock(void* context)
{
    mutex_unlock(context); /* Zephyr: k_mutex_unlock(context) */
}

static const struct x430_port rtos_port = {
    .context = &bus_mutex, .lock = lock, .unlock = unlock, .millis = port_millis,
    .delay_us = port_delay_us};

FreeRTOS: xSemaphoreTakeRecursive / xSemaphoreGiveRecursive, xTaskGetTickCount converted to milliseconds. POSIX: a pthread_mutex_t of type PTHREAD_MUTEX_RECURSIVE (see examples/host_sim/x430_host_sim.c).

docs.title: Events
docs.text:
The event X430_EVENT_BAUD_RATE arrives after the status packet of the write that changed Baud Rate (8), so the answer leaves at the old rate:

static uint8_t on_event(struct x430_device* device, enum x430_event event, void* user_data)
{
    int32_t code = 0;

    (void)user_data;
    if ((event == X430_EVENT_BAUD_RATE) || (event == X430_EVENT_FACTORY_RESET))
    {
        (void)x430_device_get(device, X430_ADDR_BAUD_RATE, &code);
        board_uart_set_baud((uint8_t)code); /* code 1 = 57600 bps, 3 = 1 Mbps */
    }
    else if ((event == X430_EVENT_BUS_WATCHDOG) || (event == X430_EVENT_TORQUE_SHUTDOWN))
    {
        motor_stop();
    }
    else
    {
        /* reboot, clear, backup restored */
    }
    return DXL2_ERR_NONE;
}

docs.title: Persistent storage
docs.text:
The EEPROM area (76-byte block) and the backup (328-byte block) are opaque byte blocks with a header and a CRC (format). The device keeps no copy of them: it reads and writes them in parts at an offset, so the hooks map directly onto a memory-mapped flash page or an I²C EEPROM:

static int nvm_read(struct x430_device* device, enum x430_nvm_slot slot, uint16_t offset,
                    uint8_t* data, uint16_t length, void* user_data)
{
    (void)device;
    (void)user_data;
    return flash_read((uint32_t)slot, offset, data, length); /* 0, or negative without data */
}

static int nvm_write(struct x430_device* device, enum x430_nvm_slot slot, uint16_t offset,
                     const uint8_t* data, uint16_t length, void* user_data)
{
    (void)device;
    (void)user_data;
    if (offset == 0U)
    {
        flash_erase((uint32_t)slot); /* a new block starts at offset 0 */
    }
    return flash_write((uint32_t)slot, offset, data, length); /* 0, or negative: Result Fail */
}

A block is read as header, payload in chunks of 16 bytes and CRC (checked before anything is taken from it), then once per register the device takes. It is written as three parts with increasing offsets — header, payload, CRC — so the last part ends at X430_NVM_EEPROM_SIZE or X430_NVM_BACKUP_SIZE; a block cut short by a reset fails its CRC and the device starts with factory values. To keep the previous block until the new one is complete, write into a second page and switch pages when the last part arrives.

A key-value store that keeps whole records only (Zephyr NVS or settings, for example) needs one buffer of X430_NVM_BACKUP_SIZE bytes (X430_NVM_EEPROM_SIZE without BACKUP) in the application: collect the parts there and store the record when the last part arrives; for nvm_read, load the record into it at offset 0 and copy from it. All devices can share that buffer when they are initialized and served from one context: a device finishes one block (it always starts at offset 0) before it or another device touches the next.

nvm_write is called from the bus context after the change. On an MCU with one flash bank an erase stalls the CPU: refuse the write (return a negative value, the host gets Result Fail) while the power stage runs, or copy the parts and write them from another thread.

docs.title: Adding the library to a CMake build
docs.text:
set(X430_MODEL xm430_w350)
set(COMPILE_DEFINITIONS X430_MAX_DEVICES=2U)  # options of x430_config.h
set(COMPILE_OPTIONS -Os)                      # flags of the library sources
include(path/to/DYNAMIXEL-X430-Control-Table-Emulator/x430.cmake)
target_link_libraries(app PRIVATE x430)
target_link_libraries(x430 PUBLIC zephyr_interface)   # Zephyr applications only

With UNIT_TESTS=ON in the project, the unit tests of this library are built too (x430_gtest) and run with the project's CTest (ctest -L x430); the x430 library itself never contains them.

In a Zephyr module, take DXL2-C from a west project instead of FetchContent with FETCHCONTENT_SOURCE_DIR_DXL2, pin it to the tag x430.cmake expects (X430_DXL2_GIT_TAG), and put DXL2-C's cmake/ folder first on CMAKE_MODULE_PATH (Zephyr has a version.cmake of its own).

docs.title: ROS 2 (dynamixel_hardware_interface)
docs.text:
The interface pings each ID, loads the model file by Model Number, writes Torque Enable and Operating Mode, programs Indirect Address blocks and reads them with Fast Sync Read (falling back to Sync Read). All of this is emulated. Points to check:

  • The Model Number must exist in its param/dxl_model/dynamixel.model. The XW430-T200 (1,280) is not listed there: use CONFIG_X430_MODEL_NUMBER_OVERRIDE=1270 or add a model file.
  • Fast reads answer for the IDs of this bus only: keep all IDs of one hardware component on the same emulator bus.
  • The Fast Sync Read answer must fit DXL2_MAX_PACKET_SIZE: 10 + devices × (bytes + 4).

docs.title: DYNAMIXEL Wizard 2.0
docs.text:
The factory baud rate is 57,600 bps, as on an X430, so the default scan finds the device. After the scan the Dashboard and the Control Table tab read the whole Control Table (addresses 0–661) in one READ of 662 bytes, which the default DXL2_MAX_PACKET_SIZE of 768 allows; below that the Wizard shows TIME OUT (Packet size).

The screenshots below were taken with DYNAMIXEL Wizard 2.0 (v2.16.4.7) and a stepper joint firmware built on this library (an STM32G431 board with a 17HS19-2004S1 stepper motor at 24 V, emulating an XM430-W350, Model Information = firmware version, voltage limits raised with an application override):

Velocity mode at the Velocity Limit. Present Current and Present PWM are written by the firmware from its current measurement and duty cycle.

Position mode during a move: the sign of Present Velocity and Present PWM follows the direction.

Control Table: the EEPROM area (pink addresses) is locked while the torque is on, as on an XM430.

Limit Settings with the factory values of that firmware.

docs.title: Without hardware: the host simulator
docs.text:
examples/host_sim/x430_host_sim.c serves simulated devices on a POSIX serial port or pseudo-terminal (Linux, macOS, WSL):

cmake --preset "X430[Examples]" && cmake --build "build/X430[Examples]"
"build/X430[Examples]/examples/x430_host_sim" --pty --link /tmp/ttyDXL --ids 1,2,3
# point DynamixelSDK or ROS 2 at /tmp/ttyDXL

docs.title: Bring-up checklist
docs.text:
1. PING with DynamixelSDK or the Wizard at 57,600 bps: the Model Number and Firmware Version come back.
  2. READ the whole table (Wizard Control Table tab): no TIME OUT.
  3. WRITE Torque Enable 1 and 0: the write hook switches the motor; Goal Position takes Present Position.
  4. Move in Position mode: Present Position and Moving follow the motor.
  5. Write an EEPROM register (Return Delay Time) with the torque off, power-cycle: the value survives (nvm_write / nvm_read).
  6. Set Bus Watchdog to 10 and stop the host: after 200 ms the motor stops and Bus Watchdog reads −1.
  7. Raise a hardware error with its Shutdown bit: the torque goes off, statuses carry the alert bit, REBOOT clears it.
  8. Change Baud Rate: the answer comes at the old rate, the next packet at the new one.

docs.title: MISRA C:2012 compliance
docs.text: This page records how the library is checked against MISRA C:2012 and every deviation from it. It covers the library code only: src/, inc/ and x430.h. The generated model table is constant data written by tools/x430_gen_model.py; the host example and the tests are not part of the library.

docs.title: Checking
docs.text:
Check Where Gate Cppcheck MISRA C:2012 addon misra-analyze, CI MISRA C:2012 Analysis Fails on any violation Cppcheck, all checks cppcheck-analyze, CI Cppcheck Analysis Report CodeQL cpp-queries codeql-analyze, CI CodeQL Analysis Report Compiler -std=c11 -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -Wconversion (-Werror in the unit tests) No warnings Sanitizers AddressSanitizer and UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer on both unit test presets No finding Manual review Pull request review Reviewer

The analysis sees the sources without the Kconfig header, so Cppcheck checks every configuration of the #if blocks; the generated model header and the DXL2-C headers are given to it as copies in <build>/x430/analysis-include.

docs.title: Current status
docs.text: Item Result Cppcheck MISRA addon 0 violations (Cppcheck 2.13.0, Ubuntu 24.04) Unit test coverage of src/ 100 % lines and branches, X430[UnitTests] and X430[UnitTestsMinimal] Deviations 2 (DEV-01, DEV-02)

docs.title: Manual review notes
docs.text: Guideline How the library complies Dir 4.1 (run-time failures) Every table access is bounded by the table size: addresses and lengths of instructions are checked before use, Indirect Address targets outside the table are ignored, packet parameters are read only within their length; sanitizers in CI. Dir 4.11 (validity of arguments) Every public function checks its pointers and the initialization of the instance before any access. Dir 4.12, Rule 21.3 (dynamic memory) No heap. Rule 8.9 (objects at block scope) No file-scope object: the only constant data are the model table and x430_sim_hooks, both used from several functions or by the application. Rule 10.4 (essential types) Build-time options may be signed literals on the command line; the code uses the unsigned copies X430_MAX_DEVICES_U, X430_REG_WRITE_SIZE_U, X430_BAUD_RATE_CODE_MAX_U. Rule 15.5 (single point of exit) One return per function. Rule 17.2 (recursion) No recursion; tools/docs/stack_usage.py fails on a call cycle. Rule 21.6 (standard I/O) No <stdio.h>; no <string.h> either (byte copies are explicit loops).

docs.title: DEV-01: Rule 11.3 (required), opaque instances
docs.text:
• Location: x430_bus_ctx_of(), x430_bus_ctx_of_const(), x430_device_ctx_of(), x430_device_ctx_of_const() and x430_sim_ctx_of() in src/x430_internal.h, the only casts from the public instance types to the private state types. Marked with cppcheck-suppress misra-c2012-11.3.
  • Rationale: The application allocates the instances (no heap, no global state), so it must know their size, but not their layout. The public struct x430_bus, struct x430_device and struct x430_sim are arrays of uint64_t of that size; the private struct x430_bus_ctx, struct x430_device_ctx and struct x430_sim_ctx hold the state. The internal types stay out of the application code and can change without breaking the API.
  • Risk control: x430_bus.c, x430_device.c and x430_sim.c check at compile time that each public type is at least as large and as aligned as its private state, and that the DXL2-C link has the size the public header assumes; a unit test checks that the public size wastes less than one word. Every public function converts the pointer before any member access and checks it for NULL and for a successful initialization (ready).

docs.title: DEV-02: Rule 11.5 (advisory), context of a callback
docs.text:
• Location: x430_handler() in src/x430_bus.c (the packet handler given to DXL2-C) and x430_sim_of() in src/x430_sim.c (the user data of the simulator hooks). Marked with cppcheck-suppress misra-c2012-11.5.
  • Rationale: DXL2-C and the hook interface pass a void* context back to the callback, the usual C way to give a callback its object without global state. The library converts it back to the type it registered.
  • Risk control: The bus registers its own private state as the DXL2-C context in x430_bus_init(); nothing else can reach these callbacks. The simulator hooks accept only an initialized struct x430_sim (the ready field is checked; NULL and an uninitialized simulator are ignored), which the application passes as x430_device_config::user_data as documented.

docs.title: Introduction
docs.text: DYNAMIXEL-X430-Control-Table-Emulator (the X430 emulator) is a C11 library that makes a microcontroller answer on a DYNAMIXEL bus like a ROBOTIS X430 actuator. It decodes Protocol 2.0 instruction packets (with DXL2-C), keeps the Control Table of the selected X430 model, enforces the rules a real actuator enforces and answers with status packets. The motor behind it can be anything — a stepper, a BLDC, a simulation: the library reaches it only through hooks, so the host tools of the DYNAMIXEL ecosystem work unchanged. DynamixelSDK (end to end) and DYNAMIXEL Wizard 2.0 (on hardware) are verified; ROS 2 dynamixel_hardware_interface uses the same instructions (points to check).

docs.title: What the library does
docs.text:
• The X430 Control Table. One of 17 models per build, generated from YAML data that the test suite compares with the ROBOTIS e-Manual tables: addresses, sizes, access, initial values and ranges, limit registers, the EEPROM lock while the torque is on.
  • Every instruction a host uses. PING, READ, WRITE, REG_WRITE, ACTION, FACTORY_RESET, REBOOT, CLEAR, BACKUP, SYNC_READ/WRITE, BULK_READ/WRITE, FAST_SYNC_READ, FAST_BULK_READ, with Status Return Level, Return Delay Time, Secondary ID and broadcast.
  • The rules around the motor. Indirect Address/Data, Bus Watchdog, hardware error shutdown and the alert bit, Startup Configuration, Drive Mode "torque on by goal update", Goal Position := Present Position on torque on, persistence of the EEPROM area and of the Control Table backup with a header and a CRC.
  • A simulator (optional) that moves the shaft with the X430 profiles, for tests and for setting up ROS 2 or the Wizard before the hardware exists.

docs.title: What the library does not do
docs.text: Concern Why it is not in the library UART, DMA and baud rate drivers Hardware-specific; the application moves the received bytes in and writes the status packets out in a callback. Motion and current control The motor is the application's; the write hook receives each accepted goal, limit and mode. Flash or EEPROM drivers The library reads and writes opaque blocks in parts through nvm_read / nvm_write; where they live is up to the application. Threads, queues, interrupts The library defines the contexts and takes an optional lock; the application decides where they run. See the integration guide. Protocol 1.0, other DYNAMIXEL series Only Protocol 2.0 and the X430 family are emulated. Another family needs its model data.

docs.title: Who it is for
docs.text:
• Firmware of custom actuators (stepper or BLDC joints, grippers) that should appear as DYNAMIXEL servos to existing host software.
  • Test benches and CI that need X430 devices without hardware (the simulator and the POSIX host example serve them on a pseudo-terminal).
  • Projects that must be reviewed or certified: MISRA C:2012, 100 % coverage, no heap.

docs.title: Key properties
docs.text:
Property Value Language C11, no warnings with -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -Wconversion Dependencies <stddef.h>, <stdint.h>, <stdbool.h>; DXL2-C 2.0.0 (fetched by CMake) Memory No heap, no global or static mutable data (.data and .bss are empty) RAM 384 B per device, 1,664 B per bus, 32 B per simulator (Cortex-M4, default options; details) Flash 10,119 B with the model table, plus 842 B of DXL2-C (Cortex-M4, -Os, all features) Stack 424 B worst case, x430_bus_receive(), with any packet size (Cortex-M4 -Os, details) Coding standard MISRA C:2012, 0 Cppcheck 2.13 addon violations, 2 deviations Tests 100 % line and branch coverage of src/ in both unit test presets (137 and 104 GoogleTest cases); model data against the e-Manual; 52 checks end to end with the official DynamixelSDK Thread safety One bus context per line, an optional lock for the live register updates; see Threading License Apache License 2.0

The library was verified on hardware in a stepper joint firmware (an STM32G431 board, Zephyr) with DYNAMIXEL Wizard 2.0; the screenshots in the integration guide come from it.

docs.title: Terminology
docs.text: Host The program that sends instruction packets: DynamixelSDK, DYNAMIXEL Wizard, ROS 2. Bus One serial line (TTL or RS-485) and the devices this firmware hosts on it (struct x430_bus). Device One emulated actuator with one DYNAMIXEL ID (struct x430_device). A dual-axis 2XL430/2XC430 is two devices. Control Table The register image of a device: EEPROM area (addresses 0–63, persistent, locked while the torque is on) and RAM area (64–661). Hook An application function the device calls: write, read, event, nvm_read, nvm_write. Live register A read-only RAM register the application keeps current: Present Position, Present Velocity, Moving and the others.

docs.title: Conventions in this documentation
docs.text:
• Registers are written with their e-Manual name and address: Goal Position (116).
  • Protocol errors are the DXL2_ERR_* codes of DXL2-C (Result Fail, Instruction, CRC, Data Range, Data Length, Data Limit, Access); library status codes are X430_OK and X430_ERR_*.
  • The example model is the XM430-W350, the default of the build.

docs.title: X430 Emulation
docs.text: This chapter describes what a host sees: the Control Table model, how each instruction is executed, the rules a real X430 enforces and how the library reproduces them, the format of the persistent blocks, and the kinematic model of the simulator with its equations. Every rule is taken from the code (src/) and checked by the unit tests in tests/unit/; the measured results come from tests/unit/gtest_x430_sim.cpp and from the DynamixelSDK check in tests/sdk/.

docs.title: The Control Table model
docs.text:
models/x430_family.yaml holds the Control Table shared by the X430 family (662 addresses, two Indirect Address blocks of 28 entries) with two variants:

Variant Models Current registers Operating modes current XM430, XH430, XD430, XW430 Current Limit (38), Goal Current (102), Present Current (126) 0, 1, 3, 4, 5, 16 load XL430, XC430, 2XL430, 2XC430 Present Load (126) only 1, 3, 4, 16

models/x430/<model>.yaml lists what differs: Model Number, variant, removed registers (LED on the XW430) and initial values or ranges. tools/x430_gen_model.py merges both, validates the result (sizes, overlaps, EEPROM below address 64, a check for every writable register) and writes x430_model_table.c with the register list and an address map (one byte per address: register index + 1, 0 = reserved).

Every register has a write check:

Check Valid values Registers (examples) range min..max ID (0..252), Return Delay Time (0..254), limits mask only the bits of a mask Drive Mode (bits 0, 2, 3), Shutdown opmode an operating mode of the model Operating Mode (11) symmetric −limit..+limit, the limit is another register Goal PWM (±36), Goal Current (±38), Goal Velocity (±44) goal position Min..Max Position Limit (52, 48) in mode 3; ±1,048,575 in the other modes Goal Position (116) indirect RAM address 64..661 Indirect Address 1–56

tests/models compares every model with a snapshot of the e-Manual control tables (size, access, area, initial value and range of every register). Differences are allowed only where the emulator deviates on purpose:

Item e-Manual Emulator Why Protocol Type (13) 1–2 2 only Only Protocol 2.0 is emulated Protocol Type initial on XW 1 2 Same; the XW description names 2 as the default Secondary ID (12) range 0–252 0–255 253–255 disable the function (as described) Bus Watchdog (98) range 1–127 0–127 0 disables and clears the error (as described) XW430-T200 Model Number 1,270 1,280 The table repeats the number of the XW430-T333; ROBOTIS tools use 1,280 ID write that collides with another emulated device accepted Data Range Error Two local devices with one ID would answer together Partial write of a multi-byte register – bytes are merged Not specified; the whole new value is checked

docs.title: Addressing and status packets
docs.text:
• A packet to an ID is executed by the device with that ID; only it answers.
  • Devices whose Secondary ID (12) equals the packet ID execute it silently; they refuse EEPROM writes and FACTORY_RESET. Values 253–255 disable the Secondary ID.
  • Broadcast (0xFE): PING is answered by every device in ascending ID order; WRITE, REG_WRITE, ACTION, REBOOT, CLEAR, BACKUP and FACTORY_RESET (not option 0xFF) are executed silently; READ is ignored.
  • Status packets of other devices on the line are ignored.
  • Status Return Level (68): 0 = PING only, 1 = PING and READ (also the group reads), 2 = all. The level written by an instruction already applies to its own answer.
  • Return Delay Time (9) × 2 µs is waited through x430_port::delay_us before each answer.
  • The alert bit (0x80) is set in the error byte of every status while Hardware Error Status (70) is not 0.
  • REBOOT and FACTORY_RESET answer first, then act. After an ID change the answer still comes from the old ID.

docs.title: Writes
docs.text:
1. A length of 0 is a Data Length Error; a range beyond the table an Access Error.
  2. Bytes written through Indirect Data are resolved to the addresses they point at.
  3. Every register the write touches is checked with its new value (the bytes of the write merged into the current bytes). Errors: Access (read-only, EEPROM while the torque is on, EEPROM through the Secondary ID), Data Range (value, limit registers, a goal while a Bus Watchdog error is active), Result Fail (Torque Enable after a shutdown). If one check fails, nothing is stored.
  4. In address order the write hook is called for each register; it may refuse, which stops the write at that register. Accepted registers are stored.
  5. If an EEPROM register changed, the EEPROM area is stored through nvm_write; a failure is reported as Result Fail.
  6. Drive Mode bit 3: a goal written with the torque off switches the torque on (through the write hook). Torque Enable 0 → 1 copies Present Position into Goal Position.

Reserved addresses read as 0 and ignore writes. REG_WRITE runs steps 1–3, keeps up to X430_REG_WRITE_SIZE bytes and sets Registered Instruction (69); ACTION runs the whole write. A Baud Rate change raises X430_EVENT_BAUD_RATE after the status packet, so the answer still leaves at the old rate.

docs.title: Indirect Address and Data
docs.text: Indirect Address 1–28 (168–222) map Indirect Data 1–28 (224–251), and 29–56 (578–632) map 634–661. An Indirect Data byte behaves like the byte it points at (size, range and access are those of the target register); a byte that points at Indirect Data itself is plain storage. ROS 2 dynamixel_hardware_interface uses this to read Present Position and Present Velocity with one Fast Sync Read; the DynamixelSDK check does the same.

docs.title: Lifecycle
docs.text:
Situation EEPROM area (0–63) RAM area (64–661) x430_device_init() Factory values, then the stored block Factory values, then the Startup Configuration REBOOT Kept Factory values, then the Startup Configuration; errors cleared FACTORY_RESET 0xFF / 0x01 / 0x02 Factory values (keep the ID / keep ID and Baud Rate) As REBOOT BACKUP 0x01 – Whole table stored, Backup Ready (147) = 1 BACKUP 0x02 (torque off) Restored except ID, Baud Rate, Protocol Type Restored except Torque Enable, Bus Watchdog

Startup Configuration (60): bit 1 restores the RAM area from a valid backup, bit 0 switches the torque on (through the write hook). FACTORY_RESET 0xFF gives the device its factory ID from x430_device_config::id — or the model default 1 when that ID is used by another device of the bus.

docs.title: Bus Watchdog
docs.text: With Torque Enable = 1 and Bus Watchdog (98) = 1..127, the device expects an instruction packet at least every \(T_{\mathrm{wd}} = 20\,\mathrm{ms} \times\) Bus Watchdog. The time since the last instruction packet is compared in x430_bus_poll() and on the next packet; when it is exceeded, Bus Watchdog reads 0xFF (−1), the event X430_EVENT_BUS_WATCHDOG fires and the goal registers answer Data Range Error until Bus Watchdog is written again. The resolution is the period of x430_bus_poll().

docs.title: CLEAR
docs.text: Option 0x01 with the magic bytes 44 58 4C 22 clears the multi-turn information of Present Position. It is refused with Result Fail while Moving (122) is 1. The event hook does the work (the simulator moves its shaft); without an event hook the library wraps Present Position into 0..4095.

docs.title: Group instructions
docs.text:
• SYNC_READ / BULK_READ: one status packet per hosted device, in the order of the request, taking turns like X series actuators on one wire (below).
  • FAST_SYNC_READ / FAST_BULK_READ: one status packet with ID 0xFE. Per device it carries [error, ID, data, CRC]; each CRC covers the packet from the header up to that point, and the last one is the packet CRC. The packet is not byte-stuffed, as DynamixelSDK expects. If the request lists an ID that this bus does not host, the bus stays silent (below).
  • SYNC_WRITE / BULK_WRITE: applied to the hosted IDs without status; a malformed BULK_WRITE is ignored as a whole.

docs.title: Several buses on one wire
docs.text:
A product may put one emulator bus on each MCU and connect the MCUs to one half-duplex wire, together with real actuators: each bus then hosts only some of the IDs of a request. Every bus hears the status packets of the others (the bus decodes them; it never answers one).

  • SYNC_READ / BULK_READ take turns. The device listed first answers at once. Every later hosted device answers only after the status packet of the ID listed just before it: at once after a device of the same bus, else when the status of that ID has been received from the wire. So the answers never overlap, as on a bus of X series actuators.
  • A missing device ends the read. If the status of the ID before does not arrive within X430_TURN_TIMEOUT_MS (default 100 ms) of the last progress of the read, or the host sends its next instruction first, the remaining hosted devices of the read stay silent. DynamixelSDK stops at the first ID that does not answer anyway, and a late answer could collide with the next instruction. A hosted device that does not answer reads (Status Return Level 0) ends the read the same way. The timeout uses the millisecond clock of the port; keep it longer than one status packet at the lowest baud rate in use plus the Return Delay Time.
  • A Fast read of several buses is not answered. The answer to FAST_SYNC_READ and FAST_BULK_READ is one packet whose segments come from all devices, chained by a running CRC; a bus cannot build the part of another one. When the request lists an ID that this bus does not host, it stays silent, and the ROBOTIS ROS 2 hardware interface falls back to SYNC_READ after 10 attempts. With all IDs on one bus nothing changes: keep all IDs of one ROS 2 hardware component on the same emulator bus to use the Fast read.

docs.title: Persistent blocks
docs.text:
The library hands the application opaque blocks; their layout is fixed so that a block of another model or a damaged flash page is detected:

Offset Size Content 0 4 Magic X430 4 2 Model Number (little endian) 6 1 Format version (1) 7 1 Slot: 0 EEPROM area, 1 backup 8 2 Payload size: 64 (EEPROM area) or 316 (the compact image of the device) 10 n Payload: the first n bytes of the compact image (the table bytes 0..63 for the EEPROM area) 10 + n 2 CRC-16 of DYNAMIXEL Protocol 2.0 (polynomial 0x8005) over bytes 0..9+n

A block with any field that does not match is ignored: the device keeps its factory values. The EEPROM block is 76 bytes (X430_NVM_EEPROM_SIZE), the backup 328 bytes (X430_NVM_BACKUP_SIZE).

The compact image is the Control Table a device keeps in RAM without its long reserved runs: for every X430 model the addresses 0–147, 168–251 (Indirect Address 1–28 and Indirect Data 1–28) and 578–661 (Indirect Address 29–56 and Indirect Data 29–56), 316 of 662 bytes. The generator writes these segments into the model table; the reserved bytes left out read 0 like every other reserved address.

docs.title: The simulator
docs.text:
The simulator replaces the motor with a kinematic model that follows the X430 profiles. It works in integer units: the shaft position \(s\) in 1/1000 pulse (4,096 pulses per turn) and the shaft velocity \(v\) in 1/1000 pulse per second, advanced in steps of \(\Delta t\) = 1 ms. The register units convert as

\[ \begin{aligned} u_v &= 0.229\,\tfrac{\mathrm{rev}}{\mathrm{min}} = 15{,}633\ \tfrac{\mathrm{mpulse}}{\mathrm{s}} \\ u_a &= 214.577\,\tfrac{\mathrm{rev}}{\mathrm{min}^2} = 244{,}140\ \tfrac{\mathrm{mpulse}}{\mathrm{s}^2} \end{aligned} \]

docs.title: Position modes (3, 4, 5)
docs.text:
With \(g\) the Goal Position on the shaft (\((\text{Goal Position} - \text{Homing Offset}) \times\) direction \(\times 1000\)), \(V\) the profile speed (Profile Velocity \(\times u_v\), or Velocity Limit \(\times u_v\) when Profile Velocity is 0) and \(A\) = Profile Acceleration \(\times u_a\), each step \(k\) computes

\[ \begin{aligned} e_k &= g - s_k, \qquad d_k = \lvert e_k \rvert \\ r_k &= \min\!\left(1000\, d_k,\ \sqrt{2 A \min(d_k, 10^9)},\ V\right) \\ v_{k+1} &= v_k + \operatorname{clamp}\!\left(\operatorname{sgn}(e_k)\, r_k - v_k,\ -\tfrac{A}{1000},\ \tfrac{A}{1000}\right) \\ s_{k+1} &= s_k + \left\lfloor v_{k+1} / 1000 \right\rceil_0 \end{aligned} \]

where \(1000\,d_k\) is the speed that arrives within one step, the square root the fastest speed that can still brake to standstill at the goal, and \(\lfloor\cdot\rceil_0\) a division truncated toward zero. With \(A = 0\) the velocity jumps to its target. When the remaining distance is not larger than the step (or below half a pulse) the shaft is placed on the goal and \(v = 0\). The square root is an integer square root (at most 32 iterations). Drive Mode bit 2 (time-based profile) is treated like the velocity-based profile.

The curve is computed by tools/docs/diagrams.py with the same integer arithmetic.

docs.title: Velocity, PWM and current modes (1, 16, 0)
docs.text: The target velocity is Goal Velocity \(\times u_v\) (mode 1), Goal PWM / PWM Limit \(\times\) Velocity Limit \(\times u_v\) (mode 16) or Goal Current / Current Limit \(\times\) Velocity Limit \(\times u_v\) (mode 0), limited to ±Velocity Limit \(\times u_v\) and ramped with \(A\) as above; the shaft advances by \(\lfloor v/1000 \rceil_0\) per step. With the torque off the velocity is 0 and the shaft holds its position.

docs.title: Live registers
docs.text:
After the steps of x430_sim_step() the simulator writes

Register Value Present Position (132) \(\mathrm{round}(s/1000) \times\) direction + Homing Offset Present Velocity (128) \(\mathrm{round}(v \times \text{direction} / u_v)\) Present Current / Load (126) Velocity change of the last step in \(u_v\), limited to Current Limit (or ±1000 for Present Load) — a rough stand-in for the effort Present PWM (124) Present Velocity / Velocity Limit \(\times\) 885 Moving (122), Moving Status (123) 1 and Profile Ongoing while the shaft turns or a Goal Position move is not done; In-Position, profile type (step, rectangular, triangular, trapezoidal) Velocity / Position Trajectory (136 / 140) The target velocity; Goal Position in the position modes Present Input Voltage (144), Present Temperature (146) From struct x430_sim_config

Direction is −1 with Drive Mode bit 0 (reverse), +1 otherwise.

docs.title: Measured
docs.text:
Scenario (test) Simulator Closed form Difference Move of 4,096 pulses, Profile Velocity 100, Profile Acceleration 20 (TrapezoidalMoveTimeMatchesTheClosedForm), \(T = d/v + v/a\) 2,920 ms 2,940.3 ms −0.69 % Velocity ramp 0 → 100, Profile Acceleration 5 (VelocityRampTimeMatchesTheClosedForm), \(t = v/a\) 1,275 ms 1,280.7 ms −0.45 %

The peak Present Velocity of the move is exactly the Profile Velocity (100). The move ends slightly early because the last steps place the shaft on the goal as soon as it is closer than one step. The tests accept ±1 %.

docs.title: Limits of the emulation
docs.text:
• Motion, current control and PID gains belong to the motor: the library stores the gains and limits, the application applies them.
  • Present Input Voltage and Present Temperature are not compared with their limits by the library: the application raises the hardware error.
  • Only Protocol 2.0; Protocol Type accepts 2 only.
  • One model per build; all devices of a build emulate the same model.

docs.title: Using the Library
docs.text: This chapter shows how to set up a bus and its devices, how the application reacts to the host through the hooks, how it keeps the live registers current and how errors come back. The UART, RTOS and flash side is in the Integration Guide; the build options are in Configuration.

docs.title: Setting up a bus and its devices
docs.text:
One struct x430_bus serves one serial line; one struct x430_device is one DYNAMIXEL ID. Initialize the bus and every device, then attach the devices:

static struct x430_bus bus;
static struct x430_device joint;

static int uart_write(void* context, const uint8_t* data, size_t length)
{
    (void)context;
    return board_uart_write(data, length);
}

int app_start(void)
{
    const struct x430_bus_config bus_config = {.write = uart_write, .port = &port};
    const struct x430_device_config joint_config = {
        .id = 11U,                  /* factory ID */
        .firmware_version = 0U,     /* 0: X430_FIRMWARE_VERSION (52) */
        .model_information = 0x00010000U,
        .hooks = &hooks,
        .user_data = NULL,
    };
    int result = x430_bus_init(&bus, &bus_config);

    if (result == X430_OK)
    {
        result = x430_device_init(&joint, &joint_config);
    }
    if (result == X430_OK)
    {
        result = x430_bus_attach(&bus, &joint);
    }
    return result;
}

x430_device_config::id is the factory ID: it is used while no EEPROM block is stored and again after FACTORY_RESET 0xFF; an ID stored by the host wins at startup. x430_device_init() loads the factory values, the stored EEPROM area (nvm_read), the RAM area and applies the Startup Configuration — which may already call the write hook to switch the torque on. Initialize a device before attaching it, never while a bus serves it. A dual-axis 2XL430/2XC430 is two devices (factory IDs 1 and 2).

docs.title: Reacting to the host: hooks
Keeping the live registers current
docs.text:
The device does not know the motor. Update Present Position (132), Present Velocity (128), Present Current/Load (126), Present PWM (124), Moving (122), Moving Status (123), Velocity/Position Trajectory (136/140), Present Input Voltage (144) and Present Temperature (146) with x430_device_set(), either periodically:

void motor_loop_1ms(void)
{
    (void)x430_bus_lock(&bus);
    (void)x430_device_set(&joint, X430_ADDR_PRESENT_POSITION, motor_position());
    (void)x430_device_set(&joint, X430_ADDR_PRESENT_VELOCITY, motor_velocity());
    (void)x430_device_set(&joint, X430_ADDR_MOVING, motor_moving() ? 1 : 0);
    (void)x430_bus_unlock(&bus);
}

or on demand in the read hook, where the lock is already held. x430_device_set() checks nothing but that a register starts at the address.

docs.title: Faults
docs.text:
Report a fault of the power stage with x430_device_raise_hardware_error():

void on_overtemperature(void)
{
    (void)x430_bus_lock(&bus);
    (void)x430_device_raise_hardware_error(&joint, X430_HW_ERROR_OVERHEATING);
    (void)x430_bus_unlock(&bus);
}

The bit stays in Hardware Error Status (70) until REBOOT and every status packet carries the alert bit. If the bit is enabled in Shutdown (63) and the torque is on, the library switches Torque Enable off, calls the event hook with X430_EVENT_TORQUE_SHUTDOWN and refuses Torque Enable = 1 with Result Fail until REBOOT.

docs.title: Using the simulator
docs.text:
Instead of a motor, a device can run the built-in model:

int sim_start(void)
{
    const struct x430_device_config config = {
        .id = 1U, .hooks = &x430_sim_hooks, .user_data = &joint_sim};
    int result = x430_sim_init(&joint_sim, &joint, NULL); /* before the device */

    if (result == X430_OK)
    {
        result = x430_device_init(&joint, &config);
    }
    return result;
}

void sim_tick_1ms(void)
{
    (void)x430_sim_step(&joint_sim, 1U); /* takes the bus lock when attached */
}

docs.title: Return values
docs.text: Code Value Returned when X430_OK 0 Success (also when the host gets a protocol error) X430_ERR_PARAM −1 NULL pointer, a value outside its range, no register at the address, no device with the ID X430_ERR_STATE −2 An instance without a successful initialization; a device that is already attached X430_ERR_CONFIG −3 Bus full, or the device ID is already used on the bus X430_ERR_HAL −4 The byte writer returned non-zero for a status packet X430_ERR_UNSUPPORTED −5 BACKUP or the simulator is not compiled in

docs.title: Common mistakes
docs.text: Symptom Likely cause Every call returns X430_ERR_STATE The *_init() function failed or was not called The host gets no answer Wrong baud rate or ID; Status Return Level 0/1; the received bytes never reach x430_bus_receive() DYNAMIXEL Wizard shows TIME OUT on the Control Table tab DXL2_MAX_PACKET_SIZE was lowered below 768: the Wizard reads the whole table (662 bytes) at once (Configuration) ROS 2 refuses the device The Model Number is not in its model files (XW430-T200); use CONFIG_X430_MODEL_NUMBER_OVERRIDE The arm jumps when the torque is switched on Present Position was not current when the host wrote Torque Enable EEPROM writes answer Access Error The torque is on (as on a real X430), or the packet used the Secondary ID The host sees the old values after a power cycle No nvm_write hook, nvm_write does not keep the parts at their offsets, or nvm_read fails Deadlock in a hook The hook called a bus function, or the lock is not recursive

docs.title: Detailed Description
docs.text:
Parts. A bus (x430_bus) decodes the instructions of one serial line with DXL2-C and answers for its devices (x430_device). A device holds the Control Table of the model selected at build time and enforces the rules of the real actuator; the application connects it to its motor through x430_hooks. The optional simulator (x430_sim) replaces the motor.

Execution model. Everything runs in one task context (an RX thread or the main loop), never in an interrupt: x430_bus_receive() with the bytes from the UART, x430_bus_poll() every few milliseconds (Bus Watchdog), and the live register updates of the application between x430_bus_lock() and x430_bus_unlock(). Hooks run inside x430_bus_receive() with the bus lock held.

Platform access is done only through x430_bus_config::write (the bytes of a status packet), the optional x430_port (lock, millisecond clock, delay) and the hooks of each device.

Initialization. Every function except the three *_init() functions returns X430_ERR_STATE for an instance without a successful initialization and calls no hook. An initialization checks every argument before it changes the instance: a refused initialization leaves the instance as it was.

docs.title: Detailed Description
docs.text:
The values come from three places, highest priority first: * a compiler definition of the X430_* macro itself (for example -DX430_MAX_DEVICES=8U); * the Kconfig header x430_autoconf.h (CONFIG_X430_* symbols), included when the build defines X430_HAS_AUTOCONF; * the defaults below.

The emulated model is not configured here: CMake generates its Control Table (x430_model_table.c) and x430_model_info.h for the model selected with Kconfig or with the X430_MODEL cache variable.

docs.title: define X430_TURN_TIMEOUT_MS
docs.text:
Longest wait, in milliseconds, for the status packet of the device before a hosted device in a SYNC_READ or BULK_READ (default 100). 

#define X430_TURN_TIMEOUT_MS `(100U)`

On a bus shared with devices of other buses (other MCUs, real servos), a hosted device answers a SYNC_READ or BULK_READ only after it has received the status packet of the ID listed just before it, like an X series actuator. When that status does not arrive within this time after the last progress of the read, the remaining hosted devices of the read stay silent. A new instruction packet ends the wait as well. The time comes from the millisecond clock of x430_port; without a clock the wait ends only with the next instruction packet. Keep it longer than one status packet at the lowest baud rate in use, plus the Return Delay Time.

docs.title: Detailed Description
docs.text: Control Table values come from the ROBOTIS e-Manual of the X430 models (https://emanual.robotis.com/docs/en/dxl/x/). Which registers a model really has is decided by its generated table: XL/XC models have no Current Limit (38) and Goal Current (102) and report Present Load at 126; XW models have no LED (65).

docs.title: typedef x430_nvm_read_hook
docs.text:
Read part of a persistent block ( x430_hooks::nvm_read ). 

typedef int(* x430_nvm_read_hook) (struct x430_device *device, enum x430_nvm_slot slot, uint16_t offset, uint8_t *data, uint16_t length, void *user_data);

The device reads a block in parts, so that it needs no buffer of its own: first the whole block in chunks (header, payload and CRC are checked), then the registers it takes from it. Return the stored bytes; where they live is up to the application.

Parameters:

  • device Device.
  • slot Block to read.
  • offset First byte, from the start of the block.
  • data Destination of length bytes.
  • length Bytes; offset + length is at most X430_NVM_EEPROM_SIZE or X430_NVM_BACKUP_SIZE.
  • user_data x430_device_config::user_data.

Return value:

  • 0 length bytes were read.
  • <0 No data: the device treats the block as missing (factory values stay).

docs.title: typedef x430_nvm_write_hook
docs.text:
Write part of a persistent block ( x430_hooks::nvm_write ), after the change; may be slow. 

typedef int(* x430_nvm_write_hook) (struct x430_device *device, enum x430_nvm_slot slot, uint16_t offset, const uint8_t *data, uint16_t length, void *user_data);

A block is written in parts with increasing offsets, from 0 to its end (X430_NVM_EEPROM_SIZE or X430_NVM_BACKUP_SIZE): header, payload (straight from the Control Table image of the device) and CRC. Start a new block at offset 0 (for example erase the flash page) and commit it when offset + length reaches the size. A block that is not written to its end fails the CRC check when it is read.

Parameters:

  • device Device.
  • slot Block to write.
  • offset First byte, from the start of the block.
  • data length bytes, opaque to the application.
  • length Bytes.
  • user_data x430_device_config::user_data.

Return value:

  • 0 Written.
  • <0 Failure: the remaining parts are not written, the host gets Result Fail.

#ifndef X430_MODEL_H
#define X430_MODEL_H

#include <stdint.h>

#ifdef __cplusplus
extern "C" {
#endif

#define X430_REG_WRITABLE 0x01U
#define X430_REG_EEPROM 0x02U
#define X430_REG_SIGNED 0x04U
#define X430_REG_GOAL 0x08U
#define X430_REG_CHECK_SHIFT 4U
#define X430_REG_CHECK(check) ((uint32_t)(check) << X430_REG_CHECK_SHIFT)

enum x430_check
{
    X430_CHECK_NONE = 0,      
    X430_CHECK_RANGE,         
    X430_CHECK_MASK,          
    X430_CHECK_OPMODE,        
    X430_CHECK_SYMMETRIC,     
    X430_CHECK_GOAL_POSITION, 
    X430_CHECK_INDIRECT       
};

struct x430_reg
{
    uint16_t address; 
    uint8_t size;     
    uint8_t flags;    
    int32_t initial;  
    int32_t min;      
    int32_t max; 
};

struct x430_indirect_block
{
    uint16_t address; 
    uint16_t data;    
    uint16_t count;   
};

struct x430_segment
{
    uint16_t address; 
    uint16_t length;  
    uint16_t offset;  
};

struct x430_model
{
    const char* name;                           
    const struct x430_reg* registers;           
    const struct x430_indirect_block* indirect; 
    const struct x430_segment* segments;        
    uint32_t operating_modes;                   
    uint16_t model_number;                      
    uint16_t table_size;                        
    uint16_t register_count;                    
    uint16_t current_unit_ua;                   
    uint8_t indirect_count;                     
    uint8_t segment_count;                      
    uint8_t axes;                               
};

extern const struct x430_model x430_model_active;

#ifdef __cplusplus
}
#endif

#endif /* X430_MODEL_H */

#ifndef X430_TYPES_H
#define X430_TYPES_H

/* ==============================================================================
 * INCLUDES
 * =============================================================================*/

#include <stddef.h>
#include <stdint.h>

#include "x430_config.h" /* first: sets DXL2_MAX_PACKET_SIZE for dxl2.h */
#include "dxl2.h"
#include "x430_defs.h"

#ifdef __cplusplus
extern "C" {
#endif

/* ==============================================================================
 * INSTANCES (FORWARD DECLARATIONS)
 * =============================================================================*/

struct x430_bus;
struct x430_device;

/* ==============================================================================
 * PLATFORM PORT
 * =============================================================================*/

typedef void (*x430_lock_fn)(void* context);

typedef uint32_t (*x430_millis_fn)(void* context);

typedef void (*x430_delay_fn)(void* context, uint32_t us);

struct x430_port
{
    void* context;          
    x430_lock_fn lock;      
    x430_lock_fn unlock;    
    x430_millis_fn millis;  
    x430_delay_fn delay_us; 
};

/* ==============================================================================
 * APPLICATION HOOKS
 * =============================================================================*/

typedef uint8_t (*x430_write_hook)(struct x430_device* device, uint16_t address, uint8_t size,
                                   int32_t value, void* user_data);

typedef void (*x430_read_hook)(struct x430_device* device, uint16_t address, uint16_t length,
                               void* user_data);

typedef uint8_t (*x430_event_hook)(struct x430_device* device, enum x430_event event,
                                   void* user_data);

typedef int (*x430_nvm_read_hook)(struct x430_device* device, enum x430_nvm_slot slot,
                                  uint16_t offset, uint8_t* data, uint16_t length, void* user_data);

typedef int (*x430_nvm_write_hook)(struct x430_device* device, enum x430_nvm_slot slot,
                                   uint16_t offset, const uint8_t* data, uint16_t length,
                                   void* user_data);

struct x430_hooks
{
    x430_write_hook write;         
    x430_read_hook read;           
    x430_event_hook event;         
    x430_nvm_read_hook nvm_read;   
    x430_nvm_write_hook nvm_write; 
};

/* ==============================================================================
 * CONFIGURATION TYPES
 * =============================================================================*/

struct x430_bus_config
{
    dxl2_write_fn write;          
    void* write_context;          
    const struct x430_port* port; 
};

struct x430_device_config
{
    uint8_t id;
    uint8_t firmware_version;
    uint32_t model_information;
    const struct x430_hooks* hooks;
    void* user_data;
};

struct x430_sim_config
{
    uint16_t input_voltage; 
    uint8_t temperature;    
};

/* ==============================================================================
 * INSTANCES
 * =============================================================================*/

#define X430_NVM_EEPROM_SIZE (X430_NVM_HEADER_SIZE + X430_RAM_START + 2U)
#define X430_NVM_BACKUP_SIZE (X430_NVM_HEADER_SIZE + X430_IMAGE_SIZE + 2U)

#if defined(UINTPTR_MAX) && (UINTPTR_MAX > 0xFFFFFFFFU)
#define X430_POINTER_BYTES 8U
#else
#define X430_POINTER_BYTES 4U
#endif

#define X430_ALIGN_UP(n, a) (((((n) + (a)) - 1U) / (a)) * (a))

#define X430_DXL2_LINK_BYTES                                                                      \
    X430_ALIGN_UP(                                                                                \
        (4U * X430_POINTER_BYTES) + X430_ALIGN_UP(DXL2_MAX_PACKET_SIZE, X430_POINTER_BYTES) +     \
            X430_POINTER_BYTES + X430_ALIGN_UP(4U, X430_POINTER_BYTES) + X430_POINTER_BYTES + 8U, \
        X430_POINTER_BYTES)

#define X430_BUS_BYTES                                  \
    (X430_DXL2_LINK_BYTES + (3U * X430_POINTER_BYTES) + \
     (X430_MAX_DEVICES_U * ((2U * X430_POINTER_BYTES) + 8U)) + 16U + DXL2_MAX_PACKET_SIZE)

#define X430_DEVICE_BYTES \
    ((3U * X430_POINTER_BYTES) + 17U + X430_IMAGE_SIZE + X430_REG_WRITE_SIZE_U)

#define X430_SIM_BYTES (24U + X430_POINTER_BYTES)

#define X430_BUS_WORDS ((X430_BUS_BYTES + 7U) / 8U)
#define X430_DEVICE_WORDS ((X430_DEVICE_BYTES + 7U) / 8U)
#define X430_SIM_WORDS ((X430_SIM_BYTES + 7U) / 8U)

struct x430_bus
{
    uint64_t opaque[X430_BUS_WORDS]; 
};

struct x430_device
{
    uint64_t opaque[X430_DEVICE_WORDS]; 
};

struct x430_sim
{
    uint64_t opaque[X430_SIM_WORDS]; 
};

#ifdef __cplusplus
}
#endif

#endif /* X430_TYPES_H */

docs.title: function x430_frame_status
docs.text:
Completes a status packet in place (no second buffer): header, id , the byte stuffing of instruction, error and data, the length field and the CRC. 

size_t x430_frame_status (
    uint8_t * tx,
    size_t capacity,
    uint8_t id,
    uint16_t count
)

The result is byte for byte the packet of dxl2_encode(). A status whose stuffed form does not fit capacity becomes a Data Length Error without data (the alert bit is kept).

Parameters:

  • tx Packet buffer: error byte at offset 8, count data bytes from 9.
  • capacity Size of tx, at least 9 + count and at least 11 bytes.
  • id ID of the answering device.
  • count Status data bytes.

Returns:

Packet length (at least 11).

/* ==============================================================================
